{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The second night she did not wait for the sea to ask. She set her hand on the sill before the light failed and let the chart open in her, every fathom of it, so that when the water came pressing it found the answers already laid out like tools on a bench. It did not like that. She felt its displeasure as a change in the pitch of the wind, a low note under the ordinary noise, and she thought of her grandmother saying that the sea was only ever curious until it was insulted.

The ring was warm from the start now. She wondered if it had ever truly been cold, or if she had simply been.

Near midnight the leaning began again, but she had learned its shape. She let her wrists go thin and did not fight the blurring. Instead she followed one line as it smeared, the shoal off the eastern point, and held that single edge sharp while the rest of the coast swam. It was like carrying a full cup across a moving deck: not by stillness, but by giving a little, everywhere but the one place that mattered.

The tower groaned. She groaned with it, and was almost glad.

Grey came sooner than she expected. The lantern still burned. On the sill there was no new mark, and she found the absence heavier than the scratch had been. He had trusted her with the reef, then. Or he had not come. She could not decide which she preferred, and let the tide take the question out with it."}
